subject: Request: temporary onboarding SLA adjustment & credit structure

From: procurement@unicomm.com
To: naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2025-05-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: onboarding SLA adjustment & credit structure

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's latency profile and the KV/cache options. Before we finalize the purchase order, our procurement and ops leads asked whether Redwood can accept a temporary relaxation of the uptime target during our onboarding period. Our go-live traffic pattern will include two weeks of heavy indexing and three weeks of go-live stabilization with spike behavior.

Specifically, we're asking whether Redwood can: 
- Allow a temporary uptime baseline of 99.5% for the first 90 days post-launch (after which we'd revert to standard terms), and
- Cap monthly service credits at the greater of $5k or 10% of monthly committed spend during that window.

We understand this is nonstandard — we're willing to sign a short amendment and escrow the credit calculation if that helps. Also attaching our internal risk note (summary).

Can you confirm if this is something Redwood can accept, and what internal approvals will be required?

Thanks,
Tanya Singh
Head of Ops, Unicomm Analytics
procurement@unicomm.com

[Attachment: Unicomm-risk-summary.pdf]

From: naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com
To: procurement@unicomm.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2025-05-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: onboarding SLA adjustment & credit structure

Hi Tanya — thanks for outlining the ask and for sharing the risk note. We appreciate the clear context on your onboarding spikes. Quick summary of what we can offer and open items: 

Proposal (conditional):
- Standard uptime baseline: 99.9% after onboarding.
- Temporary onboarding baseline: 99.5% for an initial period. We can do 60 days by default, extendable to 90 days by mutual written agreement tied to a defined stabilization checklist (indexing complete, KV cache warmed, and traffic smoothing completed).
- Monthly service credits during the onboarding window: pro-rated by minutes of unavailability using our standard credit ladder, with a cap set to the greater of $4,000 or 8% of monthly committed spend for the onboarding months.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile target of 200ms for primary routes; burst/ingestion windows may have a relaxed 95th percentile of 400ms, provided ops is notified ahead of scheduled ingestion windows or we coordinate a maintenance-like carveout for the heavy indexing.

Operational options to reduce risk:
- Recommend Dedicated pool reservation for the go-live week with burst capacity enabled (we'll quote reserved capacity pricing). This materially reduces the chance of hitting the lower uptime band.
- Prefix/KV cache pre-warm and request-level caching for ingestion paths.

Docs & next steps:
- I attached a draft amendment (Unicomm-SLA-Amendment-v1.pdf) with the temporary baseline and cap language.
- We will need Sales + Legal signoff for any credit cap changes and Finance to accept the proposed cap.

Would you be available for a 30-min call this afternoon to walk the amendment and the dedicated pool delta? If helpful, I can include our technical lead (Marissa) to go over the cache/reservation checklist.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

[Attachment: Unicomm-SLA-Amendment-v1.pdf]

From: tanya.singh@unicomm.com
To: naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2025-05-12T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: onboarding SLA adjustment & credit structure

Hi Naomi,

Thanks — that readout is helpful and we like the operational mitigations (dedicated pool + cache pre-warm). A couple of follow-ups from procurement and finance: 
- Can the monthly cap be lowered to the greater of $3,000 or 5% of committed spend? Our CFO wants a tighter cap for the initial quarters.
- We'd prefer the onboarding window explicitly state a rollback trigger based on the stabilization checklist (so we don't extend inadvertently).
- SOC 2 evidence and a summary of audit logging retention are required prior to signing the amendment.

We'll take the amendment to legal once we land on cap/length. DocuSign link would help speed signatures. Are you able to accept an escrowed credit ledger (monthly statement) that both parties can review?

Regards,
Tanya
Tanya Singh
Head of Ops, Unicomm Analytics

From: naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Fwd: Request: onboarding SLA adjustment & credit structure

Forwarding Unicomm's ask. Key asks: lower temporary uptime to 99.5% for onboarding (they want 90 days), and a lower monthly credit cap (they're pushing to $3k/5%). They require SOC 2 evidence and want credits escrowed/ledgered.

My suggested thumbs-up: we offer 60 days by default with an explicit stabilization checklist to avoid accidental extension; cap at the greater of $4k or 8% as a starting point — but finance/legal will need to sign off. Recommend we offer Dedicated pool pricing as a clear mitigation option (highly likely to reduce risk).

Can you advise whether Finance will accept the $4k/8% cap for the onboarding months and whether Legal will be okay with the escrowed credit ledger approach? Also, if we agree to 60 days instead of 90, can we keep the extension path available for their ops to request in writing?

Thanks — Naomi

Naomi — good summary. Finance is generally comfortable with a measured onboarding exception, but prefer a shorter window in practice. I approve the approach with these adjustments: 
- Make the default onboarding window 60 days (extendable to 90 only with a written stabilization sign-off from the customer and final approval from Sales Ops).
- Cap at the greater of $4,000 or 8% of monthly committed spend for those months. Finance will accept escrowed monthly credit statements reconciled at the account level.
- Legal should review the amendment language around "stabilization checklist" and "automatic extension" — avoid auto-extend clauses.

I'll loop Legal (Marissa) to take a quick look at the amendment PDF and prepare a DocuSign-ready version. Also recommend we price Dedicated pool add-on and provide an implementation checklist for cache pre-warm so the customer can see the mitigation cost vs credit exposure.

Ben Carter
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
